final.label: identifier-name-states-role

skill_entry.name: 14. An identifier states its role (members, parameters, flags, functions, labels)
skill_entry.trigger: The diff adds or renames a member, parameter, flag, function or label, and one holds. (a) Generic last token (layers, data) while the removed line or comment names the quantity. (b) The trailing comment qualifies with the identifier's kind of token but another value (per-Q versus per_b). (c) A one-to-three-letter parameter, neither a word nor role-typed, abbreviating a name the body or call site uses, ten times its hits at BASE. (d) Two flags share a stem and gate different `if` lines, or a member shares a constructor parameter's name. (e) An absolute word (indefinitely, once) bounded by a body operand, or a phase word (prepare, launch) with a differently-phased callee. (f) A workflow label cased unlike repository labels sharing a word.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE: when `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD (merged PR), use the merge-base of HEAD and the merge commit's first parent; never `<commit>~1`. Map every added line to file:HEADline with the awk command (procedures.md). 2. Bin added lines: trailing-comment declarations, `-`/`+` member pairs, bool or counter locals, signatures with one-to-three-letter parameters, absolute or phase words, `_untraced|_impl|_inner`, `labels.*.name`. 3. Per bin compare the name with: comment qualifiers (prefix and standard abbreviations match); removed tokens; same-stem siblings and their `if` lines; BASE whole-word counts (a short-name hit naming another quantity counts zero); the whole function for a bounding operand; the header access label for a wrapper split; the repository label list (network). 4. Report the proposed name in a suggestion block.
skill_entry.question: Reading only the identifier at its use site, can a reader tell what it holds, which event it is the first of, or what the function does, and does the name agree with its own trailing comment, with the names beside it in the same scope, and with the spelling the rest of the code base uses for the same quantity?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A name the diff only moves (B, MAX_B, tok_ix on PR 2287). A token with ten or more hits at BASE (tok_ix, idx, `_q`) is a convention; only (b) fires on it. A comment that expands or defines the identifier (gqa, tron-1707). A parameter whose type names the role (process_device_id), a word (pos, key), a forwarding lambda, both spellings new in the PR (q_lo, tron-4353), four-or-more-letter abbreviations. A local caching a same-named accessor. A name stating one of several guards. A wrapper split whose private header declaration shows callers inherit tracing (3769729340). A move named in the body or a reply (3001991780). The author's rename spelling. Constants (13), test names (5), typos, formatting, data files, mechanical renames.
skill_entry.finding_shape: "`<name>` (<file:line>) <holds | gates | is> <what the comment, the removed names or the body say>, but the name only says <generic noun | per_b | first>; <the comment says '<word>' | `<sibling>` at :<line> already gates <other thing> | the call site passes `<long name>`>. <Nit | a bit of a nit>: `<proposed name>`?" with a ```suggestion block when the fix is one line. For a behavior word: "this function is named '<word>' but <bounding statement at :<line>> means it <does not>, right? Should the name or the comment change?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit to minor, never blocking: 'a bit of a nit, but I prefer to see more descriptive param names ;)' (2897235803), 'definitely a nit' (3001991780), 'just a trivial nit' (3580238651), 'IMHO' (3769684790), 'I would prefer something like' (2982403509). He approves while the rename is open (PR 2103 approved at 20:13:01 after the 20:12:13 comment; PR 3302 approved 94 s after the comment). A name that contradicts the function's behavior is still a question, framed as learning ('newby-probe here :)', 2380263378), normal severity.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the enclosing function or struct at HEAD, the header declaration for a wrapper split); other files (the call site, the dominant spelling at BASE over h and src, sibling workflow files); network for the repository label list (`gh label list`); the instruction reference for an instruction operand (AMD APM vol. 3, MWAITX). PR body and replies only to learn of a planned move. Not commits, CI or runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: an identifier states its role

Common setup for this check. `base_ref=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.ref)`. When `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$base_ref` prints HEAD itself, the PR is merged: `git -C WT log --merges --format='%H %P %s' origin/$base_ref | grep <PR head>` gives the merge commit, and `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD <first parent of that merge commit>)`. Never use `<commit>~1` as BASE (on PR 3302, 57368de081~1 is the PR commit before the merged head and already holds the new workflow file). On PR 2089: base_ref hwattention_sync, merge commit 1794cdf67d, first parent b618bda79a, BASE 97f0f99674 for HEAD 57af5033da.

1. Added lines mapped to HEAD: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src .github/workflows | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3); next} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]-1; next} /^\+/{n++; print f":"n": "$0}' > added.txt` (one line per added line, `file:HEADline: +text`; 1024 lines on PR 2089, gof.hpp:79 and gof.cpp:55 verified against `git show`). Bin before reading anything: (b) declarations with a trailing comment `grep -E '\w+\s*(\{\}|= [^;]*)?;\s*//' added.txt` -> step 2; (a)/(d) a `-` member line and a `+` member line in one hunk of a header -> step 3; (d) `grep -E '\+\s*(bool|int|size_t|uint32_t|uint64_t)\s+\w+\s*(=|\{|;)' added.txt` -> step 4; (c) `grep -E '\w+\s*\(.*\)\s*(noexcept|\{|const|;)' added.txt | grep -E '\b(const\s+)?[A-Za-z_:<>]+[*&]?\s+[a-z]{1,3}\s*[,)]'` -> step 5 (8 lines on PR 2089, gof_configure twice among them); (e) `grep -E '\b\w*(indefinitely|forever|never|always|once|all|every|traced|untraced|prepare|launch)\w*\s*\(' added.txt` -> step 6; `grep -E '_(untraced|impl|inner)\s*\(' added.txt` -> step 7; `grep -E 'labels\.\*\.name|label\.name' added.txt` -> step 8.
2. Name versus own comment. Split the identifier on `_`; list the comment's qualifiers (per-X, k/v, tx/rx, first/last, HBM/host, count/base; examples, not a closed list). A comment word matches an identifier token when the token equals it, is a prefix of it of two or more letters, or is a standard abbreviation (tok/token, ix/idx/index, dev/device, hw/hardware, q/query, kv/k/v). Flag only when a comment qualifier and an identifier token are of the same kind and differ (per-Q against per_b). Skip when every comment noun expands a token, states what the flag gates, or names who uses the member (tron-1707 device.hpp attn_req, tok_ix, bypass_read_q; driver.hpp gqa; PR 2089 shard.hpp:28 `base_tok_ix // first token index`: all approved with no text).
3. Name versus removed names: for a `-`/`+` pair in one struct, `diff <(echo '<old ids>' | tr '_' '\n') <(echo '<new id>' | tr '_' '\n')`; a specific token the `+` identifier dropped and the `+` comment kept is the finding, and the proposed name restores it.
4. Name versus siblings. For each bin-(d) local take the first `_`-token as the stem; `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk 'NR>=A && NR<=B'` for the enclosing function, then `grep -nE '\b<stem>\w*\b'` and `grep -nE 'if \(<stem>\w*\)'` inside the range. Compare only pairs where both names are read in an `if (` line and gate different statements. For a member: `grep -n '<struct>(' <header>` and `git -C WT grep -n '<struct>::<struct>(' HEAD -- src` for a constructor parameter of the same name holding another thing. Two counters whose second tokens state distinct roles (dma_start / dma_done) are not a pair; a local that caches a same-named accessor (kv_cache.hpp v_ptr, tron-2693) or views a longer-named parameter (plan / plan_state, tron-4353) is not a pair.
5. Name versus repository spelling, the gate for (c). Exclude first: a dictionary word (pos, key, len), a type that names the role (process_device_id, std::shared_ptr<node_base>), a lambda or forwarding function of three lines or fewer that passes its parameters unchanged (model.hpp:773-778 on PR 2089, silent), four-or-more-letter abbreviations (n_kvheads, didx, dlen on tron-1722, silent). Then `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'A,Bp'` for the body (`<field> = <param>`, log strings) and `git -C WT grep -n '<fn>(' HEAD -- h src` for the call site arguments. Count at BASE: `for w in <short...> <long...>; do printf '%s ' $w; git -C WT grep -w -c "$w" BASE -- h src | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END{print s+0}'; done`. A short-name hit at BASE that names another quantity (hs = heap_start at src/pos/driver.cpp:738-746) counts as zero. Stop unless the long form has at least ten times the short form's hits; both spellings new in the PR (q_lo/q_hi against q_begin/q_end on tron-4353, 0 versus 0) do not fire. Report the long names in one suggestion block.
6. Name versus behavior (needs the instruction reference; cite the manual section or write Insufficient data). `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'A,Bp'` for the whole function; `grep -nE 'timeout|options|break|return|while|for \(|SUPPORTED'` inside the range. For an instruction operand cite AMD APM vol. 3, MWAITX: ECX bit 1 enables the EBX timeout in TSC cycles. Quote two inline comments on one statement that contradict each other. A name that states one of several guards (coalesce_if_unpinned_single_child, tron-2875) does not fire. For a phase word: `git -C WT grep -n '<callee>(' HEAD -- h src` to list the chain, then `grep -n -i -E 'scheduler|follow-up|later PR|moved' body.md` and the thread replies for a planned move.
7. Wrapper split: after the `_(untraced|impl|inner)` grep require `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | grep -n '<public name>\s*('` to find the old body under the public name at BASE; a helper with no BASE occurrence (on_save_impl, gof.cpp:208 on PR 2089) is new, not a split. Then `git -C WT show HEAD:<header> | grep -n -B3 '<name>_untraced'` and read whether it sits under `private:`; `git -C WT grep -n '<name>(' HEAD -- h src t` lists the callers that inherit the wrapper. Private body plus public name on the wrapper: stop.
8. Label strings (needs network): `git -C WT grep -n -E 'labels\.\*\.name|label\.name' BASE -- .github/workflows`; `gh label list --repo positron-ai/tron --limit 200 | grep -i <word>`; `grep -n '<new string>' <new workflow file>` to confirm every site spells it the same.

On PR 2089 (HEAD 57af5033da, BASE 97f0f99674): step 1 bin (c) lists src/tron/gof.cpp:55 `void gof_configure(size_t nk, size_t nh, size_t hs, float scalar)`; step 5 body :57-59 assigns `gof_params.kv_head_size = hs; gof_params.n_kv_heads = nk; gof_params.n_heads = nh;`, log :64 prints `n_kv_heads={} n_heads={} head_size={}`, call site h/tron/models/model.hpp:761 passes `n_kv_heads, n_heads, head_size`; counts at BASE: n_kv_heads 202, n_heads 92, head_size 383 versus nk 0, nh 0, hs 4 (all four heap_start, counted zero); at HEAD the 13 nk hits are the PR's own files; Wade's suggestion block 2897235803 = the long names; applied in de3bb7c7 gof.cpp:55.

On PR 2287 (open head 1a88e897e1): step 2 hit h/pos/device.hpp:85 `std::array<size_t, tron::hardware::MAX_B> tok_ix_per_b{};  // per-Q token indices`; qualifier per-Q against token per_b, same kind, different value; :84 `tok_ix  // legacy single-Q path`; MAX_B pre-existing at h/libpos.hpp:35 and bounding device.hpp:60, 61, 92, 138; Wade asked for `tok_ix_per_q` (3075717295); no reply.

On PR 2103 (021072570b): step 4 src/pos/driver.cpp:910 `bool first = true;` and :911 `bool firstcheck = true;` in wait_for_xfer_blocks; `firstcheck` gates check_for_tsc_errs at :932-935, `first` gates the 'DMA XFER saw wait time' log at :939-942; suggestion `first_tsccheck` (2842854014); head b1c1523c27 :911 `bool firsttsccheck = true;`; the `first` flag in readback_check (:852, gating :868-871) drew no comment.

On PR 3302 (dd07038737): step 8 `gh label list` (read 2026-10-06) returns `benchmark`, `bench-experiment` (lower case) beside `Skip benchmarks`, `Continuous integration`, `Run CI`, `Intel`; workflow siblings at the PR commit before the head are 'Run CI' (5 sites) and 'Continuous integration' (test-release-build.yml:16), all cased like 'Benchmark only', so the repository label list is the comparison set that reproduces 3580238651; fixed to 'dev-benchmark-only' at 57368de081 lines 6, 16, 34, 36.
final.widen_delta: New check, no existing check widened. Editor notes: (1) check 13's "Do not fire on" should hand non-constant names (members, parameters, flags, functions, labels) to check 14 instead of staying silent. (2) The "How Wade words a finding" line "He does not comment on ... the C++ guide" needs the qualifier "except descriptive-name nits (check 14)"; 2897235803 is a naming nit with a suggestion block. (3) Boundary with the merged check comment-contradicts-adjacent-code: when the comment names another existing symbol or value wrongly (prep_done for hw_prepared, 3307483528; Ra labelled O, 2771718489) or restates the identifier (3002013791), that check owns it and the remedy is the comment; check 14 owns the case where the comment correctly describes the new identifier's own quantity and the name disagrees (3075717295), and the remedy is the rename. (4) Common setup in procedures.md: add the merged-PR BASE rule (merge-base of HEAD and the merge commit's first parent) since `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD for a merged PR.

final.precedent_note: n = 8 comments over 7 PRs (tron 1485, 2089, 2103, 2233 x2, 2287, 3302, 3733), 2025-09-25 to 2026-08-12, plus the follow-up 3769729340 (2026-08-12) that concedes 3769684790. None is pasted assistant text: 2982403509 and 3001991780 on PR 2233 are Wade's own words; the 'Claude had this to say' text on PR 2233 is a different comment. All eight are inline comments, 2 as bare suggestion blocks, 5 phrased as questions. Author outcomes: changed on 2089, 2103, 2233, 3302; unknown on 2287 (open, no reply); deferred on 2233 phase-word (3001991780, 'Asking @BillBaumann to weigh in'); conceded by Wade on 3733; answered by the owner on 1485.
changes_made: Trigger (b) rewritten as a contradiction test: the comment qualifier must be of the same kind as the identifier's token with another value (per-Q versus per_b); a comment that expands, defines or names users does not fire (precision lens fix 1; refutes the tron-1707 attn_req/gqa/tok_ix/bypass_read_q false positives).

Step 2 rewritten with a token-matching rule (equal, two-letter-or-longer prefix, standard abbreviation tok/ix/dev/hw/q/kv) and the qualifier list marked as examples (executability lens fix 5 folded with precision lens fix 2; clears PR 2089 shard.hpp:28 base_tok_ix).

Trigger (c) kept at one to three letters (precision lens: do not widen; tron-1722 n_kvheads/didx/dlen silent) and narrowed with the executability lens conditions: not a dictionary word (pos, key), type not role-naming (process_device_id, shared_ptr<node_base>), no forwarding lambda (model.hpp:773-778), and the ten-fold BASE count as the gate (precision lens fix 3 and 4).

Step 5 counts moved to BASE with the rule that a short-name hit naming another quantity counts zero; the 'On PR 2089' numbers replaced by BASE 97f0f99674 counts 202/92/383 versus 0/0/4 (hs = heap_start, driver.cpp:738-746), HEAD counts kept only as the note that the 13 nk hits are the PR's own (executability lens fix 6; verified in this run).

Trigger (d) limited to two forms: flags sharing a stem that each gate a different `if`, or a member colliding with a constructor parameter; caching locals (kv_cache.hpp v_ptr, tron-2693) and views of a longer-named parameter (plan/plan_state, tron-4353) excluded (precision lens fix 5).

Trigger (e) word list closed (absolute: indefinitely, forever, never, always, once, all, every; phase: prepare, launch, traced, untraced) and conditional names stating one of several guards excluded (coalesce_if_unpinned_single_child, tron-2875) (precision lens fix 6).

Trigger (f) now compares with repository labels sharing a word (`gh label list`: benchmark, bench-experiment lower case) or sibling workflow strings; the label list was read 2026-10-06 and resolves the former open question (facts lens fixes 2, 3, 4; verified in this run).
Inherited-convention count rule added to do_not_fire: ten or more whole-word hits at BASE (tok_ix, idx, `_q`); only (b) can still fire (precision lens fix 7).
Boundary with comment-contradicts-adjacent-code stated in widen_delta (precision lens fix 8).

Common setup added for merged PRs: BASE = merge-base of HEAD and the merge commit's first parent; `<commit>~1` banned; 57368de081~1 relabeled as the PR commit before the merged head (executability lens fixes 1 and 10; merge commit 1794cdf67d verified in this run).

Step 1 replaced by the awk mapping command producing file:HEADline and a triage line binning added lines by trigger (executability lens fixes 2 and 3; gof_configure found at gof.hpp:79 and gof.cpp:55 in this run).
Step 7 requires the public name to exist at BASE before calling a hunk a wrapper split (on_save_impl on PR 2089 is a new helper) (executability lens fix 7).
Step 4 given a selection command for flags and counters and the rule that only pairs both read in `if (` lines compare (executability lens fix 8).
Steps 6 and 8 marked as needing the instruction reference and the network, with Insufficient data as the fallback (executability lens fix 9).

3769729340 described as conceding the reason 6 min 22 s after 3769684790 at the private declaration heap_v2.hpp:416, not as withdrawing (facts lens fix 5; timestamps 19:29:45Z and 19:36:07Z verified).

residual_risks: The ten-fold BASE count threshold for (c) rests on one firing case (PR 2089: 202 versus 0) and two silent cases (tron-4353 q_lo 0 versus 0; tron-3756 idx 174 versus index 366 at HEAD); a PR where the long form leads by three to nine times is undecided.

The generic-noun list in (a) (layers, data, tmp, flag) comes from one corpus hit (2982403509) plus common words; the precision lens found 0 (a) hits on 15 silent PRs, so its false-positive rate is untested beyond that.
Trigger (b)'s author outcome is unknown: PR 2287 is open with no reply, so whether the per-Q rename is accepted in this code base is not established.
The precision probe covered 15 of the 48 silent PRs (the four largest diffs in full plus 11 h/ and src/ touching PRs); the other 33 silent PRs were not run.
The repository label list for (f) was read on 2026-10-06, not at the comment date 2026-07-14; labels added or renamed since cannot be excluded.
